leads.summary: A margin on only the side the current bar does not touch disables the default gap but leaves the bar flush
leads.consequence: With a top bar, bar.floating=true, Hyprland gaps_out=10 and [bar] margin="0 0 10 0", hasMargin treats bottom=10 as an active theme margin and floatsInGap becomes false. windowMargins ignores bottom on a top bar, leaving all four effective window margins zero. The bar does not lift off the top edge, although the explicit floating switch is on; moving the bar to bottom suddenly applies 10 px. The same problem is mirrored for each of top/bottom and left/right. Decide whether to test active margins by bar position or to use Hyprland fallback when the theme margin is confined to an unused side.
leads.triage: published as new finding after Opus follow-up confirmation

leads.summary: A live edit of Hyprland's user looknfeel.lua leaves the floating bar on cached gaps and radius
leads.consequence: The supplied user config config/hypr/looknfeel.lua allows changing general.gaps_out and decoration.rounding, and Hyprland can be reloaded with hyprctl reload. Style reads getoption only on initial startup, a window-no-gaps toggle-file event, or theme IPC (shell.qml:1589). A direct live edit/reload of the user's Hyprland config does not invalidate gapsOutEdges or cornerRadius, so a bar already floating on 10 px gaps remains at the old 5/10 px margins when windows switch to a different gap. Restarting the shell, toggling window-no-gaps or applying a theme refreshes it. Add a refresh for Hyprland config reloads or qualify the docs' live-derived claim. Source-confirmed, no desktop runtime was available.
leads.triage: dropped: quattro adds Style.refresh on Hyprland configreloaded (re-runs gaps and rounding probes), so not present after merge

leads.summary: Open #13137 conflicts at [bar] parser: resolving the hunk in either branch alone loses a documented key family
leads.consequence: #13137 adds numeric icon-slot, icon-canvas, icon-font and status-slot overrides, whereas the reviewed head accepts only numeric size-horizontal, size-vertical and radius, with a separate raw margin list. Both PRs are diverged, not stacked, and the Style.qml three-way merge has one conflict. Keeping this PR's whitelist while adopting #13137's docs/tests discards all four new numeric options; keeping #13137's generic parseInt branch alone collapses this PR's CSS-style multi-side margin list. Preserve the raw margin case and the generic numeric branch in the eventual merge.
leads.triage: not published: conflict with #13137, same author's own series; ordinary rebase

leads.summary: Dependent #13140 no longer contains this PR's current commit history, and its old copy collides with the current head
leads.consequence: #13140 says it needs #13138 and #13139 and includes their commits, yet read-only compare of #13140 head 1624a87 to this head dfc1fab is diverged. A three-way merge of Bar.qml at their common base returns three conflict hunks, including the --inset sample argument concatenated with the pill-blend arguments. Treat #13140 as a dependency to rebase or deliberately reconcile after this force-pushed head and #13139, not as an already stacked PR; otherwise a naive conflict choice loses either inset contrast sampling or pill blending.
leads.triage: not published: #13140 is the author's dependent PR, diverged after force-push; ordinary restack

leads.summary: Alternative open #13569 writes incompatible floating-zone, window-size and margin policies for the same bar.floating setting
leads.consequence: The two independent open PRs share bar.floating but #13569 makes a larger transparent anchored window, sets a Normal exclusive zone unconditionally and animates its child bar. #13138 makes the window bar-sized, uses layer-shell margins and retains Auto outside the in-gap case. Git merge-file shows five conflicts in Bar.qml, including the mode/zone and all four margins. Merging both implementations piecemeal risks doubled reserve or incorrect bar placement; choose one window geometry and reservation policy.
leads.triage: published as Related PR note in Details

leads.summary: If the independent Apple-notch height PR #13478 is combined, the in-gap exclusive zone remains based on unfloored barSize
leads.consequence: #13478 (and its alternate #13641) changes a notched Apple top bar's implicit height to max(barSize,notchFloor), for example 32px on a stock 26px bar. If both branches are resolved so this PR's floatInGap mode survives with that height floor, its exclusiveZone still uses 26 minus edge margin. With 10px gaps, top margin 5 and zone 21 reserve 26px, while the visible bar window extends 5+32=37px from the screen edge; the notch-sized bar can overlap the window allocation. This is conditional because the PRs currently conflict and there is no merged runnable head. Pass the actual per-screen thickness into the reservation calculation when combining them.
leads.triage: not published: conditional on combining with notch PRs #13478/#13641

leads.summary: Open bar-reservation host #11887 snapshots only barSize, not a floating theme margin
leads.location: #11887 shell/services/BarReservation.qml: snapshot.size and shell/bar-reservation/shell.qml: exclusiveZone; shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:1277-1307
leads.consequence: If #11887 is integrated with this PR, its reservation host sets a zone equal to bar.barSize and switches the interactive window to ExclusionMode.Ignore after acknowledgement. A theme margin of 20 on a top bar with barSize 26 and gaps_out 10 requires this PR's bar-sized window to clear 46px from the screen edge, but the separate host reserves only 26px. The 20px shortfall consumes the intended 10px gap to tiled windows and potentially overlaps by 10px. The host protocol must carry the effective anchored-edge margin (or full desired reserved depth), and its reservation surface/zone must use it when floating with theme margins. The merged runtime is hypothetical until the branches' conflicting exclusionMode lines are resolved.

leads.summary: Open margin/radius PR #9725 ships an explicit default radius=0 that disables this PR's Hyprland-derived rounding
leads.consequence: #9725 adds uncommented [bar] margin=0 and radius=0 to the generated shell.toml for every theme. If those defaults survive when both diverged PRs are integrated, Style.applyShellValues stores radius=0, this PR tests barOverrides["radius"] !== undefined, and its floating bar uses radius zero instead of Hyprland's decoration:rounding. Thus every default-generated theme forces a square floating bar even when Hyprland rounds windows. Keep default radius unset/commented or explicitly distinguish template default from user override when reconciling. Conditional on future merge, not demonstrated on a merged head.
leads.triage: not published: #9725 template radius=0 is superseded here by commented template; conditional on merging #9725 separately

leads.summary: Changed wallpaper color tests permit vertical floating bars to ignore their insets
leads.consequence: The changed test exercises top, bottom and horizontal end insets but never left or right bar positions. In a sandbox, a mutant that forces a left crop back to x=0 and a right crop back to width-barSize passes every shipped color assertion (test exit 0) even though a left bar inset 20px against a two-tone wallpaper returns #101010 instead of #ffffff. Add left/right contrasting-band cases to protect bin/omarchy-bar-text-color:119-128.
leads.triage: not published: pre-existing test gap from earlier commit, low value

leads.summary: Bar-widget contract fixtures omit the newly documented barMargins field
leads.consequence: Both fixture fakeBar QtObjects define barSize but no barMargins, whereas PluginBarApi adds barMargins and Bar.qml binds it. Thus the runtime contract harness cannot model a floating widget reading bar.barMargins, and it will neither assert its value nor represent the actual public API. The separate bar-test.sh:312-318 merely regexes the declaration and binding. Add the field to both fakeBar fixtures and a widget-side assertion for a nonzero margin (or a dedicated QML contract case). Source-only test-fidelity lead, no compositor test run.
leads.triage: dropped: contract fixtures are fakes; low value

leads.summary: The user-facing top-bar manual still omits the floating bar setting
leads.consequence: The manual explains bar position, transparency, hiding and every shell.json bar key in its sample but does not tell readers about bar.floating or [bar] margin/radius. This PR updates docs/omarchy-shell.md, the plugin README and agent skill, but leaves the main end-user top-bar guide without the feature. Mention the config/theme switch and link to the detailed shell guide (not an omarchy bar floating command, which this head does not implement). #13140 would add a CLI command and manual coverage if rebased/merged.
leads.triage: not published: manual omits floating; feature documented in docs/omarchy-shell.md; low value

flags.claim: A far-edge-only theme margin disables floating
flags.why: Floating is not disabled. With a far-edge-only margin, BarModel.barFloating returns true. That is why the bar gets a radius. What the margin removes is the offset: all window margins are 0, so the bar sits flush. With "floating": true it also suppresses the in-gap float. With bar.floating false the bar is flush and square, which is expected.
flags.disposition: real error: fixed (heading now 'keeps a floating bar flush')

flags.claim: "floating": true no longer moves it into the gap
flags.why: Minor. 'no longer' suggests this revision changed the behaviour. It did not. hasMargin, barFloating, barMargins and floatsInGap are unchanged from ced6275 to dfc1fab; the only BarModel.js change is the NO_MARGINS export. The behaviour is what the floating switch does with any theme margin.
flags.disposition: real error (minor): fixed ('does not move' instead of 'no longer moves')

flags.claim: the comment ... still says Auto can pick up an explicit zone, which contradicts Quickshell and the new Bar.qml comment
why: 'Contradicts' is too strong. Quickshell's setter does switch Auto to Normal (wlr_layershell.hpp:148-153), so 'Auto can pick up an explicit zone' is a fair description of the old wiring, where the zone binding always ran. The new Bar.qml comment (1277-1280) states the same setter behaviour.

My own final.md ('Quickshell's Auto never reads the stored zone ... the new Bar.qml comment states the opposite rationale') is the source of this overstatement and is corrected here.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `dfc1fab`, the five points from the [previous follow-up](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13138#issuecomment-5852615714) are resolved ([author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13138#issuecomment-5866111054)); one new low-impact defect was found.

Resolved: popout/toast value tests, `PluginBarStateApi.barMargins`, `gaps_out` wording, property lists.

### A far-edge-only theme margin keeps a floating bar flush

`BarModel.hasMargin` checks all four sides of `[bar] margin`; `windowMargins` uses only the touched edges. A top bar with `margin = "0 0 10 0"` sits flush yet rounded (when a radius applies), and `"floating": true` does not move it into the gap. **Impact:** low; no shipped theme sets `margin`.

**Suggested change:** Check only the touched edges in `barFloating`, `floatsInGap` and `barMargins`, passing the position to the first two.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at dfc1fab)</summary>

Each block goes after the line `assertEqual(bar.floatsInGap(false, noMargin), false, 'a flush bar reserves as it always has')` in `test/shell.d/bar-test.sh`. The file's own `bar`, `gaps` (12 on every side) and `noMargin` are in scope. Run with `bash test/shell.d/bar-test.sh`. Add one block at a time, because the file stops at its first failure.

Block 1: a flush-sitting bar is rounded.

```js
// A theme margin only on the edge a top bar does not touch leaves the bar
// flush, so it should stay square like any flush bar.
const farEdge = { top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 10, left: 0 }
const farEdgeFloats = bar.barFloating(undefined, farEdge)
assertDeepEqual(bar.windowMargins('top', bar.barMargins(farEdgeFloats, farEdge, gaps, 'top'), 26, false), noMargin, 'a top bar with a bottom-only theme margin sits flush')
assertEqual(bar.barRadius(farEdgeFloats, undefined, 8, 26), 0, 'a top bar that sits flush stays square')
```

Actual output at `dfc1fab` (exit 1; earlier `ok` lines omitted):

```text
ok - a top bar with a bottom-only theme margin sits flush
expected: 0
actual:   8
not ok - a top bar that sits flush stays square
```

Block 2: `bar.floating: true` does not float the bar in the gap.

```js
// bar.floating true with a theme margin that touches none of the bar's
// edges should float the bar in the gap, as with no theme margin.
const farEdge = { top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 10, left: 0 }
const switched = bar.barMargins(bar.barFloating(true, farEdge), farEdge, gaps, 'top')
assertDeepEqual(bar.windowMargins('top', switched, 26, false), { top: 6, right: 12, bottom: 0, left: 12 }, 'bar.floating true floats a top bar in the gap when the theme margin is only on its far edge')
```

Actual output at `dfc1fab` (exit 1; earlier `ok` lines omitted):

```text
expected: {"top":6,"right":12,"bottom":0,"left":12}
actual:   {"top":0,"right":0,"bottom":0,"left":0}
not ok - bar.floating true floats a top bar in the gap when the theme margin is only on its far edge
```

The expected values are one reading of the docs ("a flush bar stays square", "Turn it on with `"floating": true`"). The docs do not say which rule wins when the margin is non-zero only on an edge the bar does not touch.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Each of the previous follow-up's popout, toast and binding edits, in its current form, now fails `bar-test.sh`.
- `exclusiveZone` is written only while the bar floats in the gap. Quickshell 0.3.1's setter forces `Normal`, and the `Binding` with `RestoreNone` never writes for a flush or hidden bar (source reading plus a model of the state changes, not a running shell).
- `PanelGeometry.js` and `NotificationLogic.barClearance` give the same results as the code they replaced in 240 popout and 40 toast cases. Flush bars match the base.
- The move preview lands where the bar window does in all 72 cases checked.
- The eight files also changed on `quattro` merge without conflicts, and `bar-test.sh` passes on the merged tree.

**Optional test improvement:** of the move preview's geometry, the check covers only `x` (plus the start of the radius call). Each of these edits to `Bar.qml` still passes `bar-test.sh`: the preview `y` ignoring the margin, `width` ignoring the margins, and the radius ignoring the theme `[bar] radius`. This check, added after the existing move-preview assertion, passes at `dfc1fab` and fails on each edit:

```js
assert(
  /y: modelData === "bottom" \? parent\.height - edgeSize - edgeMargins\.bottom : edgeMargins\.top/.test(barSource) &&
  /width: edgeVertical \? edgeSize : parent\.width - edgeMargins\.left - edgeMargins\.right/.test(barSource) &&
  /height: edgeVertical \? parent\.height - edgeMargins\.top - edgeMargins\.bottom : edgeSize/.test(barSource) &&
  /radius: BarModel\.barRadius\(root\.floating, Style\.barOverrides\["radius"\] !== undefined \? Style\.bar\.radius : undefined, Style\.cornerRadius, edgeSize\)/.test(barSource),
  'the move preview places and rounds every edge like the bar'
)
```

**Optional:** the comment on `BarModel.exclusiveZone` (`BarModel.js:273-282`) still justifies the `inGap = false` branch, but the zone is now written only while the bar floats in the gap (`exclusiveZone(true, …)`), so that branch and its two tests (`bar-test.sh:171-172`) cover code nothing calls.

**Related PR:** #13569 also adds a `bar.floating` setting, with a different window size and exclusive-zone approach, in the same `Bar.qml` code.
</details>
